item.title: Trump says he’s ready to meet Xi, Putin on the sidelines of the APEC summit: What’s on the agenda?
item.description: US President Donald Trump is open to meeting his Russian and Chinese counterparts at next month’s APEC summit to discuss denuclearisation rather than the Ukraine war. The Putin-proposed meeting remains unconfirmed but could anger Kyiv and its allies.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) expressed his willingness to meet with his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, but highlighted that the meeting would focus on denuclearisation efforts rather than ending the Ukraine war.Trump’s proposed meeting with Xi, Putin: What’s on the agendaTrump told reporters, "I would do it — not so much for Ukraine, because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine," and added, "We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization. We would schedule a meeting based on the denuclearization, and that’s a very positive thing for the world," Bloomberg reported.While there is no final confirmation of such a meeting, Trump has suggested that it could happen in Beijing during his scheduled visit to China in November for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit and talks with Xi on the sidelines.Addressing reporters, he said, “If they’d like to have it, I think it would be held in China. He just left here,” referring to Xi’s recent visit to Washington. “If President Xi wants to have it, I’d have it. I’m sure we’re talking about other things like trade too, but yeah, I would do that.”There is also no official confirmation of the proposed meeting’s agenda. However, according to AFP, when pressed on whether he would discuss Ukraine at the summit, Trump said he would do "whatever I can do to end the war."Putin proposes three-way meeting with Trump, Xi: Here’s what the Kremlin saidThe US president’s remarks came a day after The Wall Street Journal reported that Putin had proposed a three-way meeting with Trump and Xi in November to discuss the Ukraine war and negotiate an end favourable to Moscow.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said: "Given that all three heads of state might potentially attend a summit in China, the topic of such a hypothetical meeting has indeed been mentioned."Peskov added, "No substantive proposals or agreements, neither regarding the meeting itself nor its potential agenda and content, have been discussed or put forward by anyone".The proposal was reportedly made by Putin during his 9 October phone call with Trump. A potential three-way meeting between Putin, Trump and Xi in China would mark a big step for the Chinese president amid his continued efforts to elevate Beijing’s role as a diplomatic power broker.While sources told The Wall Street Journal that Russian officials had proposed the idea to China through diplomatic channels and that Beijing had indicated its willingness, provided the US president was on board, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said she had no information about a possible meeting.The remarks come as Trump has recently softened his tone towards Putin while directing sharper criticism at Ukraine.Trump softens stance on Putin, steps up criticism of UkraineDuring the same phone call in which Putin reportedly floated the idea of a three-way meeting, the US president discussed Russian diesel supplies to the US and subsequently announced a deal. In a Truth Social post, Trump said Russia had agreed to immediately supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel to the US, followed by another 500,000 tonnes in November and an additional one million tonnes "immediately thereafter."A week later, he further softened his stance on Russia by announcing a waiver of Russia-related sanctions under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, citing national interest.Amid this, the US president has ratcheted up his criticism of Ukraine and its leader, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, accusing him of not doing enough to end the war as Kyiv targeted Moscow’s energy infrastructure. In the last few weeks, Trump has called on Ukrainians to appoint a new president and accused Zelenskyy of using money from Europe and former President Joe Biden to continue his war efforts.The meeting remains unconfirmed, and it remains to be seen whether Xi will endorse the proposal amid concerns over growing bonhomie between China, Russia and the US

item.title: Trump thanks ‘legendary’ friend Elon Musk for pledging SpaceX shares to every American child through Trump Accounts
item.description: Donald Trump thanked Elon Musk for pledging one SpaceX share to every American child next year through Trump Accounts. The proposed donation could be worth about $10.7 billion, though details of how the shares will be distributed remain unclear.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump on Monday (local time) thanked billionaire Elon Musk after Musk announced plans to donate shares in his company SpaceX to millions of American children through the Trump administration’s flagship "Trump Accounts" initiative.In a social media post, Trump wrote, "A BIG THANK YOU to our legendary friend, ElonMusk, for his incredible generosity in giving SpaceX Stock to millions of American children through TRUMP ACCOUNTS! This is exactly what was envisioned when we created TRUMP ACCOUNTS — bringing together the GREAT PRIVATE SECTOR, Elon and so many more, to invest in our children, by far our greatest and most important asset, and give every American Child a piece of the American Dream."Musk commits shares to American children: What we knowHis remarks came after SpaceX founder Musk wrote in a post on X, “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many.”According to Bloomberg, Musk has agreed to distribute the stock through the Trump Accounts initiative, though he has not disclosed how the donation would be structured. Citing a source, the report said he decided to proceed after the White House announced the creation of tens of millions of accounts through automatic enrolment. Earlier this month, the White House said every American child under 18 with a valid Social Security number now has a Trump Account.Estimates from the US Census Bureau show that the US has around 72 million children, which would make Musk’s donation worth about $10.7 billion at the current share price.Musk joins the list of high-profile Trump Accounts backersThe SpaceX founder’s planned donation adds another high-profile name to the list of Trump Accounts backers. Billionaires including Michael and Susan Dell and Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio have previously pledged funds.The announcement comes nearly three months after the US president said in July that he expected Musk to contribute to the Trump Accounts programme. Around the same time, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell announced that she and her husband had gifted SpaceX stock to Trump Accounts for more than 2 million children in the US.What are Trump Accounts?According to the official website, Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children under the age of 18.Established through a tax and spending bill that Trump signed last year, the programme provides $1,000 each to eligible American children born between 2025 and 2028. It allows families, government programmes and private-sector donors to contribute funds and equities directly to eligible children’s accounts. The aim is to give children under 18 an early financial foundation and a stake in the country’s enterprise.Under the programme, money in eligible accounts stays invested until recipients reach adulthood, giving it the potential to grow over time. Since opening on 4 July, the accounts have received more than $4.5 billion, including $2.6 billion in philanthropic contributions, $1.3 billion in initial $1,000 seed contributions and over $600 million from relatives and friends. According to reports, the accounts are expected to receive further contributions soon.Family and friends can contribute up to $5,000 a year to each child’s account. Employers may provide up to $2,500 annually, which counts towards that limit. Eligible children can also receive philanthropic contributions, while more than 70 companies have pledged to set up workplace contribution programmes.(with agency inputs)
